ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two slanted lines r and s, and they have the same arrow markings, indicating r ∥ s; another slanted line q passes through r and s, and is a transversal. Angle 3 is located at the upper intersection, below line r and to the right of transversal q; angle 7 is located at the lower intersection, above line s and to the left of transversal q. Reasoning: Because r ∥ s, and q is a transversal, ∠3 and ∠7 are alternate interior angles, and alternate interior angles are equal. Therefore 4y + 30 = 7y + 6. Solving gives 30 - 6 = 7y - 4y, that is, 24 = 3y, so y = 8.

raw_record.question_text: Use the figure to find the indicated variable. Find $y$ if $m \angle 3 = 4y + 30$ and $m \angle 7 = 7y + 6$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: lines r and s have matching arrow markings, so they are parallel, and line q is a transversal crossing both. Angle 3 is an interior angle below line r on the right side of q, while angle 7 is an interior angle above line s on the left side of q. These are alternate interior angles, so they are congruent. Use the text-given expressions m∠3 = 4y + 30 and m∠7 = 7y + 6, set 4y + 30 = 7y + 6, and solve for y.
